title: BSKDL Kurzschrift Einformige Wort- und Wortstammkürzungen Contract

formalRules.summary: The source assigns standalone word meaning to 53 Braille signs.
Ten Braille signs are deliberately not given standalone word meanings because their isolated tactile position is not considered sufficiently reliable.
AN, EIN, ER, ES, ICH and IN use their Lautgruppenkürzung signs when functioning as independent words.
sourceWitnesses: an ein er es ich in

formalRules.summary: Standalone ICH is written out when followed by punctuation that can be read as an ordinal-number sign.
An independent word consisting of a Vollschrift Lautgruppenkürzung receives an Aufhebungspunkt in Kurzschrift.
sourceWitnesses: Eigenständigen Wörtern, die aus Lautgruppenkürzungen der Vollschrift bestehen

formalRules.summary: Two-form Lautgruppenkürzungen may not be used standalone.
sourceWitnesses: Die zweiformigen Lautgruppenkürzungen dürfen nicht alleinstehend verwendet werden

formalRules.summary: §4.3.1 defines nineteen one-form contractions restricted to standalone use.
The §4.3.1 contractions are not used with prefixes, suffixes or in word compounds.
When a §4.3.1 word appears in an ineligible derived or compound form, it is written out or represented by another applicable contraction.
§4.3.1 contractions remain applicable when joined to apostrophized words, except for IHM.
IM is written out when it meets a hyphen, for disambiguation.
sourceWitnesses: "Im" wird beim Zusammentreffen mit einem Bindestrich

formalRules.summary: §4.3.2 defines twenty-two one-form word contractions usable standalone.
sourceWitnesses: Die folgenden Kürzungen sind als eigenständige Wörter verwendbar

formalRules.summary: When a §4.3.2 word contraction is extended or occurs in a word compound, Point 2 is prefixed to identify it.
sourceWitnesses: Werden sie erweitert oder stehen sie in Wortverbindungen

formalRules.summary: Prepositions from this group also receive Point 2 when combined with contracted words.
When connected with apostrophized words, §4.3.2 contractions are used without the Point-2 announcement.
BEIM, NICHTS, VOM, ZUM and ZUR are explicitly deferred by the source to the two-form contraction rules in §4.4.
§4.3.3 defines IHR, SEIN and WAR.
IHR, SEIN and WAR may be used standalone or under their stated word-initial conditions without Point 2.
At word start, IHR and SEIN may contract only before E or I.
At word start, WAR may contract only before EN or ST.
§4.3.4 defines HATT, HÄTT and WELCH.
HATT, HÄTT and WELCH are used standalone, with endings, or in word compounds without an announcement.
sourceWitnesses: sowohl alleinstehend als auch in Wortverbindungen

formalRules.summary: §4.3.5 defines six one-form word stems that require an extension.
sourceWitnesses: nur in Verbindung mit einer Erweiterung gekürzt

formalRules.summary: The six §4.3.5 stems are eligible only when a qualifying extension is present.
sourceWitnesses: nur in Verbindung mit einer Erweiterung gekürzt

formalRules.summary: As an independent word without ending, or with an apostrophe, a §4.3.5 stem must be written out.
The Ergänzungsstrich shown in the §4.3.5 inventory represents the required ending and is not the one-form contraction cell itself.
sourceWitnesses: Der Ergänzungsstrich steht für die jeweils erforderliche Endung

formalRules.summary: WÜRD is not used in WÜRDIG/UNWÜRDIG because the resulting sequence would collide with the two-form contraction for ÜBRIG.
